title: Payment Arrangements — Missed Entries Owed From Before a Suspension
content:
## The rule in force

A miss whose pre-suspension grace had run out by the date missed-installment counting stopped is still owed on the installment history and is recorded once, as the missed entry of the pre-suspension installment.

This concerns plans under Payment Arrangements that were suspended for a hardship hold: a miss that had already ripened before counting stopped does not lapse because the plan was suspended. It stands as one missed entry on the plan's installment history, for the one pre-suspension installment it belongs to, and it is recorded once.

## What recording the missed entry does

Ridgeline adds a missed entry for the named installment to the arrangement's installment history, carrying that installment's scheduled due date (read off the arrangement's schedule) and today's date as the date it was recorded. The missed entry moves no money, so the amount still scheduled under the arrangement is unchanged. The consumer and the agent can afterwards see the missed entry on the installment history.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `record_missed_installment_d21cca89`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_id` | The payment plan reference number (the identifier) of the arrangement, as returned by the payment arrangement lookup for the consumer | Identifier string |
| `installment_number` | The number of the installment recorded as missed | Non-negative integer; 0 is the down payment, 1 the first regular installment |

## Return

On success the tool returns a record rendered as text with `missed_entry_reference` (the reference of the missed entry recorded), `plan_id`, `installment_number`, `due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the installment's scheduled due date), `recorded_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today) and `status`, always `missed_entry_recorded`, which shows the entry is on the history.

When no arrangement matches the reference given, the tool returns "No payment plan found for" followed by that reference, and nothing is recorded.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

Naming installment 5 of a monthly arrangement whose schedule puts installment 5 on 20 February returns a due date of 20 February, today's date as the recorded date, and the status `missed_entry_recorded`; the arrangement balance is the same before and after.
